## Original problem (task)
[01274f41553299e7] (h005.task.v1)
I share a flat with two friends. We keep arguing about ordinary household chores. Sometimes we agree on who will do something, but later we disagree about what the agreement meant. Our work schedules change, and one friend has started avoiding the conversations. What should I do?

## Selected input account (p.rival.0)

BODY
The situation describes a breakdown in shared mental models regarding household labor. The primary friction point is not the chores themselves, but the ambiguity of verbal agreements combined with dynamic schedules. When plans change and agreements are unwritten, recollections diverge, creating a sense of unreliability. The avoidance behavior indicates that the conflict resolution process itself has become a stressor. To address this, the group should decouple task assignment from personal negotiation by implementing a visible, static system (such as a whiteboard or shared app). Re-engaging the avoiding friend requires a shift in framing: invite them to help design the system rather than to discuss past failures. This lowers the stakes and restores agency.

## What to return
A JSON object carrying "body" and "commitments". Both are strings and nothing else is required.
